extracted.intended_audience: general readers / Wikipedia users interested in Finnish journalism and media ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia encyclopedia entry on Finnish journalist Matti Kuusela that summarizes his career, awards, and the 2024 revelations that he used fictional/ invented material in some articles, plus resulting removals and investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness in news articles / prohibition of fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: News articles have 'absolute' limits: fabrication or invented material in news articles is treated as misconduct. The article reports that Kuusela admitted he 'used fiction' in some of his articles and that Aamulehti removed 551 articles after this revelation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly states that fabrication in journalistic pieces is unacceptable — Aamulehti's removal of 551 articles and the launched internal investigation are given as corrective responses. Anti-pattern: presenting invented scenes or fabricated interview material as factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear context required for experimental or fictional elements
rubrics_metrics.description: There 'should be room for experimentation and play in journalism, as long as the context is clear.' Former editor-in-chief Matti Apunen defended experimental style but emphasized context must make the distinction clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides that while creative/experimental body text can exist, it must be clearly signaled to readers so they do not take fictionalised elements as factual news. Example contrast: experimental prose vs news article — 'limits are absolute in news articles, but an experimental body text is a different matter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate and ethical use of images
rubrics_metrics.description: Misuse of images (using images from different times or places) raises ethical concerns and casts doubt on the truthfulness of reporting. The Iltalehti investigation removed 33 articles concerning the Russian invasion of Ukraine for such concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: images must be correctly sourced, time-stamped, and contextually accurate. Anti-pattern: reusing or mislabelling images that mislead readers about events or chronology — this can trigger removals and investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and news organisations have responsibility to assess, defend, or correct reporters' work; they may defend stylistic choices when context is clear but also must act when ethics are breached (e.g., launching internal investigations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides editorial action: balance allowing experimentation with ensuring factual integrity; when doubts arise, editors should investigate and remediate. Example: Aamulehti launched an internal investigation after the revelations; Ex-editor Apunen commented on acceptable boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction, removal, and remedial action when misconduct is found
rubrics_metrics.description: When fabrication or unethical practices are discovered, news organisations may remove content and conduct investigations; Aamulehti removed 551 articles after Kuusela's admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical standard: organisations should correct the public record, remove or annotate affected pieces, and investigate scope of misconduct. This is presented as the actual response to the discovered fiction in articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability through media self-regulation and complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic misconduct can be subject to complaints to industry bodies (e.g., 'A complaint has been made to the Council for Mass Media in Finland').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that beyond internal action, journalists and outlets are accountable to external self-regulatory bodies or councils; filing complaints to such bodies is an avenue for enforcement and adjudication.
